story.soThat: I receive distilled knowledge from large conversation sets
story.tasks: - Task 1: Implement memory compilation service (AC: #1, #3) * Add jarvis.memory.compile module with compile_memories() function * Query PostgreSQL for conversations within time range (--since filter) * Aggregate conversation content for LLM summarization * Call LLM to generate insight summary (pattern identification, key themes) * Format output as structured Markdown with metadata headers * Write to ~/.jarvis/knowledge/insights/{{date}}-insights.md - Task 2: Add CLI command for memory compilation (AC: #1) * Add jarvis memory compile command in src/jarvis/cli/memory.py * Accept --since parameter (e.g., '7d' or ISO-8601 date) * Optional --output parameter to override default insights directory * Display progress and summary (conversations processed, tokens used, cost) - Task 3: Integrate cost tracking and LLM routing (AC: #2) * Use existing LLM provider infrastructure (if available) or stub cost tracking * Log provider name, model, input/output tokens, and cost_usd * Store cost data in PostgreSQL LLM usage tables (Story 2.1 schema) * Emit structlog events with cost/provider metadata - Task 4: Auto-ingestion of compiled insights (AC: #3) * After writing insight Markdown, automatically trigger jarvis memory add * Tag insights with domain="jarvis-insights" for filtering * Ensure insights are searchable via jarvis memory search --source jarvis-insights - Task 5: Cron configuration and error handling (AC: #4) * Document cron job example in docs/cron-jobs.md or README * Add graceful error handling (LLM API failures, database unavailable) * Log errors to structlog with severity levels * Exit codes: 0 for success, 1 for recoverable errors, 2 for fatal errors - Task 6: Tests (AC: all) * Unit tests for compile_memories() with mocked LLM and DB * Unit tests for CLI command argument parsing * Integration test: compile recent conversations, verify Markdown output * Integration test: verify compiled insights are ingested and searchable

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. Given the cron job spec in docs, When `jarvis memory compile --since 7d` runs, Then it aggregates conversations, summarizes patterns via LLM, and writes Markdown to `~/.jarvis/knowledge/insights`. 2. Given the compilation job completes, When logs are reviewed, Then they include cost + provider data for auditing. 3. Given compiled insights exist, When they are stored, Then insights are saved as ingestion-ready Markdown documents that can be re-queried via the memory search API. 4. Given the cron schedule is configured, When the job runs automatically, Then it executes without manual intervention and handles errors gracefully.

doc.title: Epic 2 — Story 2.5
doc.snippet:
As a strategist, I want automated weekly insight jobs, So that I receive distilled knowledge from large conversation sets.
Prerequisites: Story 2.4 Technical Notes: Reuse FR4.4 cron example; integrate with cost router for budget awareness; store compiled insights as ingestion-ready docs for re-query.
Acceptance Criteria: - Given the cron job spec in docs, When `jarvis memory compile --since 7d` runs, Then it aggregates conversations, summarizes patterns via LLM, writes Markdown to `~/.jarvis/knowledge/insights`, And logs include cost + provider data for auditing.

doc.title: Architecture
doc.snippet:
llm_providers: - name: openrouter type: free_tier api_key: ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY} - name: together type: free_tier api_key: ${TOGETHER_API_KEY} - name: openai type: paid api_key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY}
Cost-First Routing: Maximizes free LLM tiers (OpenRouter, Together AI, etc.) before touching paid subscriptions, using simple "run until depleted, switch" routing with API-driven usage tracking.

doc.title: Architecture
doc.snippet:
Python Code: - Modules/Packages: lowercase_with_underscores (e.g., rag_engine.py, llm_router.py) - Classes: PascalCase (e.g., RAGEngine, LLMRouter, CouncilOfRicks) - Functions/Methods: snake_case (e.g., generate_embedding, route_to_provider) - Constants: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (e.g., DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE, MAX_RETRIES)
CLI Commands: - Top-level: jarvis {command} (e.g., jarvis ask, jarvis chat) - Subcommands: jarvis {noun} {verb} (e.g., jarvis memory add, jarvis agents list) - Flags: --kebab-case (e.g., --max-sources, --output-format)

artifact.reason: Memory ingestion pipeline for auto-ingesting compiled insights. Use ingest_file() to add insights Markdown to Qdrant with domain="jarvis-insights". Returns IngestionResult with chunks/points written. Supports custom embed_fn and domain tagging.

Configuration infrastructure for LLM providers. ProviderConfig tracks provider name, type (free_tier/paid), priority, model, and api_key_env. Settings.providers list used for cost-first routing. Load settings from config/settings.yaml.

PostgreSQL ORM models for conversations, messages, and LLM cost tracking. Conversation has UUID primary key, user_id, created_at (UTC). Message has role, content, agent_persona, cost_usd, provider, model, token_count. LLMProvider tracks free-tier/paid providers with quota limits. LLMUsageLog stores per-message usage.
artifact.implementation:
class Conversation(Base): """Top-level conversation container.""" __tablename__ = "conversations" id: UUID = Column(PGUUID(as_uuid=True), primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4) user_id: Optional[str] = Column(String(255), nullable=True) created_at: datetime = Column(DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=func.now()) messages: List["Message"] = relationship("Message", back_populates="conversation")
class Message(Base): """Individual message in a conversation.""" __tablename__ = "messages" id: UUID conversation_id: UUID role: str # user | assistant | system content: str agent_persona: Optional[str] cost_usd: Optional[Decimal] provider: Optional[str] model: Optional[str] token_count: Optional[int]
class LLMProvider(Base): """LLM provider registry for cost-first routing.""" __tablename__ = "llm_providers" id: int name: str # "openrouter", "together", "openai" type: str # "free_tier" or "paid" priority: int quota_limit_tokens: Optional[int] usage_count: int

story-context.constraints: - LLM integration: If LLM router infrastructure doesn't exist, stub cost tracking for now; prioritize basic functionality over full cost routing - Cost tracking: Store provider, model, token_count, cost_usd in PostgreSQL LLMUsageLog (Story 2.1 schema) - Insights directory: Default to ~/.jarvis/knowledge/insights/, create if doesn't exist - Markdown format: Include front matter with metadata (date range, conversation count, cost, provider) - Query conversations: Use SQLAlchemy to query Conversation and Message tables within time range - Auto-ingestion: Call ingest_file() directly with domain="jarvis-insights" after writing Markdown - Cron compatibility: Support headless execution, log to files, proper exit codes - Error handling: Graceful degradation for LLM API failures, database unavailable - Domain tagging: Use "jarvis-insights" domain for compiled insights (distinct from "jarvis-core" and "jarvis-conversations") - Structlog: Log metadata only (conversation_count, time_range, cost_usd, provider, duration_ms); avoid logging conversation content - Time parsing: Reuse _parse_since() helper from memory.py for '7d' format and ISO-8601 - Knowledge base context: Current memory has 6,755 points (4 jarvis-core + ~4,989 jarvis-conversations); insights will add to this collection

interface.name: jarvis memory compile
interface.parameters: --since: Time range (e.g., '7d' or ISO-8601 date) [required] --output: Override default insights directory [optional] --collection: Qdrant collection name (default: "knowledge") [optional]
interface.description: Compiles conversations from specified time range, generates LLM summary, writes Markdown to insights directory, auto-ingests for search. Returns exit code 0 for success, 1 for errors.

interface.name: compile_memories
interface.signature: compile_memories(since: datetime, until: Optional[datetime] = None, output_dir: Optional[Path] = None) -> CompilationResult
interface.description: Core compilation service. Queries conversations, aggregates content, calls LLM for summarization, formats Markdown, writes to file, triggers auto-ingestion. Returns CompilationResult with file path, conversation count, cost data.

interface.name: ingest_file
interface.signature: ingest_file(path: Path, collection_name: str = "knowledge", domain: Optional[str] = None) -> IngestionResult
interface.description: Existing ingestion function. Call with domain="jarvis-insights" to ingest compiled insights into Qdrant. Returns IngestionResult with chunks/points written.

interface.name: Conversation.query
interface.description: Query conversations within time range. Join with Message to get all content for aggregation. Filter by created_at column (timezone-aware UTC).

interface.name: LLMUsageLog
interface.signature: LLMUsageLog(message_id=..., provider=..., model=..., input_tokens=..., output_tokens=..., cost_usd=...)
interface.description: Store LLM usage data for compilation job. Track provider, model, tokens, and cost_usd for auditing.

tests.standards: Follow pytest configuration in pyproject.toml; separate unit vs integration tests. Unit tests mock external dependencies (LLM APIs, database, file I/O); integration tests require Docker services (PostgreSQL, Qdrant). Use pytest fixtures for database sessions and Qdrant clients.
tests.locations: - Unit tests: tests/unit/memory/test_compile.py (new), tests/unit/cli/test_memory_compile.py (new) - Integration tests: tests/integration/memory/test_compile_integration.py (new)
tests.ideas: - AC1: Unit test compile_memories() with mocked database and LLM; verify Markdown output structure with front matter; test --since parameter parsing ('7d' and ISO-8601 formats); verify output file naming (date-based). - AC2: Unit test cost tracking logs; mock LLMUsageLog insertion; verify structlog events include provider, model, cost_usd, token_count; test that logs don't contain conversation content (privacy). - AC3: Integration test auto-ingestion; compile conversations, verify ingest_file() called with domain="jarvis-insights"; search via jarvis memory search --source jarvis-insights and confirm insights are returned. - AC4: Unit test error handling (LLM API failure, database unavailable); verify graceful degradation, proper exit codes (0/1/2); test cron compatibility (headless execution, no interactive prompts). - Edge cases: Empty time range (no conversations), LLM rate limiting, oversized aggregation (token limits), insights directory permissions. - Performance: Mock LLM latency; verify compilation completes within reasonable time; test batching if conversation count is large. - Markdown format validation: Verify front matter YAML structure; check metadata fields (date_range, conversation_count, cost_usd, provider); validate Markdown syntax. - Time range filtering: Test boundary conditions (since = now, since = 1 year ago); verify timezone handling (UTC); test until parameter (optional).
